blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Advertising & MarTech. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Ad and martech businesses trade on identity, measurement and trust: signal loss (cookie deprecation, ATT), clean-room measurement and consent architecture decide whether targeting survives the privacy era — and whether spend proves incrementality.

items: Third-party identifiers deprecate; first-party identity graphs inconsistent across systems.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Decentralized Identity & Verifiable Credentials, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Identity resolution, Audience activation, Measurement/incrementality) on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel. Governance inherits the sector frame — GDPR/ePrivacy/ATT-class among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Credentials users carry: portable, privacy-preserving verification for workforce and customers.
On-chain transparency, operationalized: analytics, Travel Rule and MiCA-aligned controls.
Permissioned networks for multi-party truth: governance, consensus and integration done institutionally.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
